code.modal: modal_apps/x13_naming.py (setup, features, owl, jev: JevService + caller)

question: Name SAM 3 object cards without a per-object VLM call at run time and without fine-tuning; measure the share that still needs a VLM and the accuracy of what is named without one, held out by video.

data.unit: the object card (3D-merged track); up to 5 views per card (the card's best views, then the largest outlines >= 5 keyframes apart); per view a 384 px tight crop (box + 10 %, squared) and its mask; the best view's 1.6x crop with a white-over-black outline (judge.som) for the decider; crops cut from the run's own MP4 blob and its densified outlines layer
data.labels: Gemini's open name on the card (identity.decided_by == 'gemini open name': 1,531 cards) -> cards.canonical class (else '~' + head noun, a class outside the taxonomy) -> cards.FAMILY; an offline label source, 0.81 / 0.88 right / right-or-close on the audited items, not truth
data.truth: the 119 agent-labelled held-out identity items (runs/mvp2-results/identity-heldout, mvp2/identity, blind), matched to the warm cards by id + box centre within 0.3 m (identity_study.score_final's rule; 119 of 119 matched); graded with identity_study.grade
data.lightning-3585: not used: its names come from the older SAM 2 pipeline with no SAM 3 word votes, so the SAM 3 rules could not be calibrated on it

protocol.held_out: every score is on a video whose labels were never used: the bank is the other two videos' Gemini-labelled cards, every threshold and the nested choice of the kNN key / zero-shot key come from the other video(s) only; rotated over the three videos and reported per video
protocol.thresholds: fitted, not trained: per rule the lowest score whose accepted set on the training video(s) reaches the target agreement with Gemini's class (>= 20 items); the cluster cut is the largest one whose copied names reach the target; no gradient step anywhere

fit_scopes.same domain: the other video of the same domain family (Sam's Club <-> Walmart); ME340 has no shop-floor partner, so its 'same domain' fit is the pooled one

protocol.gemini: not called at run time; where the cascade says 'needs VLM', the card's recorded Gemini name stands in for the answer and is what the bank keeps
protocol.hardware: features, OWLv2 and Jev-Omni: one A100-80GB each (isolated model benchmarks, not the 2-GPU production container); the Jev service in its own container, called from a separate CPU container (the core's stand-in)

owlv2-base.note: the card calls it a research output

models.licence_source: each model card's own README front matter, read in the container (setup and the Jev service); the SAM 3 words are the pipeline's existing SAM 3 votes (SAM License, commercial use allowed)

b_detector.match: OWLv2 box IoU >= 0.5 with the mask's box on each view; best score per class per view, mean over views

jev.caller: a CPU Modal container (the core's stand-in) calling the service container through Modal's function calls, same region

spend_usd.note: app wall time x (A100-80GB + cores + GiB) list prices from fast_report.instrument.PRICE; image builds not included; the cost ledger was not edited

comparison_gemini.held_out_audited_right_right_or_close: 0.81 / 0.88 (119 items, warm call); per video ME340 0.74/0.89 (62), Sam's Club 0.89/0.89 (28), Walmart 0.90/0.90 (29) as graded here

conclusions: The SAM 3 word vote is already the best free namer: 0.69 class agreement with Gemini over all cards (Walmart 0.87, Sam's Club 0.69, ME340 0.17), 0.62 / 0.77 on the audited items against Gemini's 0.81 / 0.88. Its words come from the one Gemini vocabulary call per video, which stays.

A cross-video label bank does not transfer between these three site types: kNN against the other two videos gets 0.15-0.25 class agreement for every encoder (0.59-0.72 at family level), and only 30 % of ME340's classes exist in the other videos at all. The bank's value is inside a video: kNN over the video's other cards reaches 0.79 class (DINOv2-L plain+masked, upper bound) and 0.76 with only the earlier cards named.

Encoders: DINOv2-L (plain+masked, mean of the views) or PE-Core-L (masked) as the kNN key, picked by the nested fit on every fold. In-video they match the current SigLIP 2 base key on class agreement (0.79 vs 0.74-0.79) and do better on the audited items (0.73 / 0.82 vs 0.58-0.66 / 0.68-0.77). Zero-shot over the 102 taxonomy words is weak with every encoder (best 0.33 class, PE-Core-L masked) and only serves as an agreement vote. OWLv2 with the taxonomy words, matched to the SAM 3 masks: 0.39 class, 82 % of cards matched; when it agrees with the SAM 3 word the pair is 0.83 / 0.90 precise on Sam's Club / Walmart, 0.36 on ME340.

Jev-Omni over retrieved candidates (median 8-11 options, Gemini's class among them for 79 % ME340 / 97 % Sam's / 96 % Walmart) is not a namer here: forced choice 0.33 class (0.49 / 0.67 audited), it never answers 'none of these' (0 of 1,596), and even p >= 0.95 is 0.62 precise on 12 % of cards. No fit reached a target, so it routed 0 cards in every cascade. Service latency: 0.076 s a question of GPU time batched by 8; 0.10 s a question round trip in 64-question requests (1.6 s of each 2.4 MB request is the hop); one question alone 0.50 s round trip for 0.11 s of compute; 45 s cold start; 22.9 GiB.

What works is SAM 3 word + a second opinion, then in-video clusters verified by the SAM 3 word: tier 1 accepts the SAM 3 word when zero-shot/OWLv2 or the cross-video bank agrees, or when its own vote share clears a fitted cut; the rest is clustered in the video (DINOv2-L), one VLM call per cluster medoid, and the answer is copied only to members whose SAM 3 word gives the same class (0.94-0.95 class agreement on the copies at the class >= 0.80 points; 0.80-0.90 where the cut came from another domain). Copying without that check was 0.42 on Walmart.

VLM share and accuracy, held out (fitted on retail for retail): at class >= 0.80 Sam's Club needs the VLM for 0.3 % of cards and Walmart for 2.8 % (audited final names 0.86/0.93 and 0.83/0.86 vs Gemini alone 0.89/0.89 and 0.90/0.90, n 28 / 29); at class >= 0.90 Sam's Club 11 % and Walmart 44 % with 0.89/0.93 and 0.93/0.93 (at or above Gemini). The 5-10 % target is reachable for retail; the price of the cheapest point is 3-7 points of 'right' on 28-29 items.

The shop floor (ME340) has no reliable cheap signal: with retail-fitted cuts at 0.80 it sends 37 % to the VLM but the names it keeps are 0.45 / 0.69 right (the video drops to 0.55 / 0.74 from Gemini's 0.74 / 0.89); at 0.90 it sends 85 % and stays near Gemini (0.69 / 0.84). There is no second shop-floor video to calibrate on, so a new domain's first video should go to the VLM.

Pooled thresholds across domains fail both ways: Walmart at class >= 0.90 pooled sends 82 % to the VLM (ME340's poor SAM 3 words set the SAM 3 cut), and ME340 at 0.80 pooled accepts wrong names. Calibrate per domain family.

Bank growth over all six orders of the three videos (empty start, the bank keeps the VLM answers only): the order barely matters (Walmart 28 % -> 24 %, ME340 38 % -> 35 % with accuracy 0.55 -> 0.52 at class >= 0.80 pooled; same-domain cuts are flat), because the savings come from within-video structure, not from a bank of other site types. Same-type videos (several Walmart walks) were not available to measure the cross-video curve.

Never write names accepted without a VLM back into the bank: the first design (stream, every final name written back, accept on the in-video vote share) collapsed to 0.2 % VLM and 0.03 class agreement, because one early neighbour is a 100 % vote.

Blind agent audit of cheap names that disagree with Gemini (class >= 0.80 same domain, 64 sampled, 6 unclear): Sam's Club cheap right/close/wrong 15/7/1 vs Gemini 22/0/1 (most disagreements are box / merchandise / stacked-boxes synonyms); Walmart 8/2/10 vs 9/7/4 (the unverified cluster copy spread 'shelf' to bags); ME340 6/3/6 vs 7/4/4.

Latency of the cheap path per card on one A100 (batched): DINOv2-L plain+masked 10.2 ms, PE-Core-L masked 15.2 ms (zero-shot vote), OWLv2 12.9 ms (0.052 s a keyframe, 102 queries), kNN 0.02 ms, clustering 0.33 s for Walmart's 720 cards (CPU).
caveats: Gemini's names are the class labels for agreement numbers; the audited items (119) and the 58 blind-labelled disagreements are the only truth, and n is 28-62 per video, so a difference of 3-7 points is 1-2 items.

Jev's options use the in-video bank of earlier cards with Gemini's labels (not the cascade's own names) so one question per card serves every fold; its answers did not affect any cascade because no Jev cut was ever fitted.
The VLM share counts objects; a medoid's answer is Gemini's recorded name for that card, so cluster copies inherit Gemini's errors.
The in-video step assumes the VLM answers for the medoids arrive before the copies are made (one extra round of latency per video: ~13 s a 14-object Gemini request in the mvp2 runs).
All three videos come from the same click-MVP runs; the SAM 3 vocabulary is per video from one Gemini call; a fixed taxonomy vocabulary for SAM 3 was not tested (it changes the masks as well).

files.not_kept_here: dataset.pkl (322 MB crops) and features.pkl (125 MB embeddings) stay in the session scratchpad; scripts/x13_naming.py build rebuilds the crops from the mirrored runs
